note: Track guitar-melodies (guitar-scales), step 5: a tune in D Dorian made from a four-note motive, ended on the root over a drone, then played over a Dm7 to G7 band. missing: the tune book behind the melody shape is major only, so there is no written modal tune to play from tab; the player makes one up.

exercise.title: Make up a Dorian tune
exercise.why: A tune sounds Dorian when it rests on the root and passes through the raised 6th, so a short motive that ends on one and touches the other keeps the mode however you turn it round.

cells.text:
The panel below spells a short motive in D Dorian, then the same four notes reversed, mirrored and rotated. Play the Motive row on the neck under the panel, in the position with {{1}} on the A string.
Then play the Reversed row and the Mirrored row, until you can play each one straight after reading it.

Press Play below to start the drone. On the neck below, make up a two-bar tune that passes through the ringed {{6}} and ends on {{1}}.
Play it until it comes out the same twice, then change one note.

Press Play below to start the band, which moves between Dm7 and G7. Play your tune over it, then answer it with a second tune that starts on another note.
When G7 comes round, try holding the ringed {{6}}: it is the 3rd of G7, so the Dorian note is the chord's own note there.
